Aave receipts registered in copied Balancer pools
Research date: 29 September 2026. Read-only inventory at PulseChain chain 369, block 27,659,393,
hash 0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275.
Finding and coverage
The bounded factory census contains 17 direct Aave linear pools, nine distinct wrappers and six
underlying assets. Four wrappers refer to the sampled Aave V3 pool: DAI, USDC, USDT and WETH. Five
refer to Aave V2: DAI, USDC, USDT, FRAX and TUSD. This is an inventory of exact registered token
addresses, not a claim that all wrappers are presently redeemable or that their inputs came through
Portal.
Nine historical canonical Aave/ERC-4626 factory families returned 38 pool creation events. All returned
creations precede the PulseChain fork boundary; the latest is block 17,231,795. Their presence is
inherited infrastructure, not proof of post-fork deployment. Other sampled pools use Sturdy, Morpho, Idle
or mock receipts; an Aave-shaped interface alone does not make them direct claims on the sampled
Aave pool. Custom factories outside this list remain outside coverage. The census does not enumerate
native deployments on an unidentified pARB execution network.
Exact wrapper identities
The wrapper's aT oken getter, the aT oken's pool/underlying getters and Balancer Vault registration agree
for each entry. V2 wrapper symbols can resemble the aT oken symbol itself; names alone are insufficient
to identify a wrapper.

V3 reserve coverage and Portal status
The sampled V3 reserve list contains WETH, wstETH, WBTC, USDC, DAI, LINK, AAVE, cbETH, USDT, rETH,
LUSD, CRV, MKR, SNX, BAL, UNI and LDO. All 17 configurations encode an unbacked mint cap of zero at
the pinned block. DAI, USDC, USDT and WETH have direct V3 wrappers in this census; no direct V3
wrapper was found for the other 13 within the nine surveyed factories. This is a bounded negative
finding, not proof that no such wrapper exists anywhere.
Portal belongs to V3. A V2 wrapper does not accept a V3 aT oken merely because both correspond to DAI
or USDC. The matched V3 wrappers are structurally relevant to Portal because Portal issues their
ordinary aT okens, but the observed zero caps and historical event search do not establish live Portal
issuance. The Aave history study (Appendix 2) supplies that distinction.
Reproducibility and limits
Maintained call manifests are Research/experiments/parb_factory_pools_20260929.json, 
parb_factory_wrappers_20260929.json, parb_wrapper_matches_20260929.json and parb_wrapper_registered_20260929.json.
They run with the read-only Research/scripts/probe_pulsechain_routes.py collector. Recorded responses,
creation receipts and source references are under ignored artifacts/parb-wrapper-inventory-20260929/. Root
review reconciled the nine wrapper links and all 17 Vault registrations directly from those responses and
decoded the 17 cap fields; this is not a second independent RPC observation.
Factory coverage: 20211208-aave-linear-pool, 20220404-erc4626-linear-pool-v2, 20220425-unbutton-
aave-linear-pool, 20220817-aave-rebalanced-linear-pool, 20221207-aave-rebalanced-linear-pool-v3,
20230206-aave-rebalanced-linear-pool-v4, 20230206-erc4626-linear-pool-v3, 20230409-erc4626-linear-
pool-v4 and 20230410-aave-linear-pool-v5. Factory catalogue provenance is Balancer deployments
commit b55dc2b. The asset/share interface is defined by ERC-4626. The deployed V3 DAI wrapper
implementation is available from the PulseChain source endpoint.
Public records were collected and the checks described above completed. A further automated review
did not complete. The inventory therefore does not have a completed independent review.
